title: GlobColour Icechunks
description: A dataset of global ocean-color satellite observations — chlorophyll-a and related biogeochemical parameters — derived from the Copernicus GlobColour product and repackaged as Icechunk-format chunked array stores for cloud-native access via a virtual store on Source Cooperative.

## README.md
# globcolour-Icechunks

This is an icechunk for [Copernicus globColour products](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/OCEANCOLOUR_GLO_BGC_L4_MY_009_104/description). Note Copernicus provides a Zarr lazy load of its data with:

```
import copernicusmarine
ds = copernicusmarine.open_dataset(
    dataset_id="cmems_obs-oc_glo_bgc-plankton_my_l3-multi-4km_P1D",
)
```

The icechunk provides an alternate access via a virtual store on Source Coop (AWS us-west-2). This will be faster in the US but slower, sometimes much much slower, in the EU and slower than using Copernicus' JupyterHub which is on CloudFerro in the same region as their data.

```
import icechunk as ic # need icechunk > 2
import xarray as xr

url = "https://data.source.coop/fish-pace/globcolour/cmems_obs-oc_glo_bgc-plankton_my_l3-multi-4km_P1D"
storage = ic.http_storage(url)
repo = ic.Repository.open(storage)
auth = {p: ic.credentials.HttpAccess for p in repo.config.virtual_chunk_containers or []}
store = repo.reopen(authorize_virtual_chunk_access=auth).readonly_session("main").store

ds = xr.open_zarr(store, consolidated=False, chunks=None)
ds
```
Use `create_default_indexes=False` in `open_zarr()` to circumvent the high I/O cost associated with creating the coords. Doesn't seem to affect xarray much. This will be particularly noticeable when I/O latency is high, e.g. when outside of US. The icechunk is in AWS us-west-2.
